_meta.title: Maturity structure of marketable Treasury debt
_meta.source: Treasury Monthly Statement of the Public Debt; Joint Economic Committee monthly debt update (Jun 2026 average maturity); Peter G Peterson Foundation for instrument shares
notes: The 30-year bond is the longest instrument issued, so nothing outstanding today was issued before 1996.
But average maturity is about 71 months, roughly six years. Roughly a third of debt matures within twelve months.
This is why rate rises after 2021 repriced the whole stock within a few years. It is the causal link to the net interest chart.
Savings bonds (Series EE and I) reach final maturity at 20-30 years and are non-marketable; excluded from these figures.
